newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper caught in range, may edge lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper caught in range, may edge lower.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices are forecast to remain in a tight range on Monday but the bias may be to the downside, analysts said.
Even so, the $2,375-$2,420 a tonne range was likely to contain most of the day's price action, they said.
COPPER
Analysts were looking for fairly narrow range trading for copper after it completed an inside day on July 4, when the U.S. markets were closed for Independence Day.

"The market could break either way. On the upside a breach of $2,420 signals a breach of important fanline resistance at $2,440, while if $2,395 breaks, a test for the fourth time of fanline support at $2,375 is likely," said Harry Creates at brokers Amlagamated Metal Trading.
Friday was quiet and offered few new guidelines as business was confined to weekend book-squaring in the recent narrow $2,395-$2,420 range.
That range could remain largely intact today but the bias was slightly to the downside, analysts said.
The broader $2,440-$2,380 range was likely to hold, with the tendancy towards the lower end, where a breach would introduce $2,350-$2,355 and key support from the uptrend line, they said
At 0715 copper was indicated at $2,400/$2,405, a couple of dollars under Friday's close.
ALUMINIUM
Little movement was seen in aluminium on Friday, but support emerged at $1,597 after speculative selling in the morning ring pushed the price through $1,600.
Analysts said the market was likely to move lower in the near term despite its close on Friday at $1,606/$1,607.
Buying was forecast at the fanline support of $1,597, which held on Friday, then at the 10-day moving average of $1,591.
Further support should be available at $1,587 and $1,577, they said, while on the upside resistance was still pegged at $1,612, followed by $1,620 and $1,628.
At 0715 aluminium was indicted at $1,604/$1,607 barely changed from Friday's close.
--Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
